children.translated_text: Having bowed to the Arhats, and having completed the instruction on words together with its ancillary sections,
I set forth a garland of names that are conventional, derivational, and mixed.
Words without etymological derivation, such as <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, are conventional names.
Derivation is connection; it arises from relation to a quality, an action, or an association.
From a quality come names such as <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>; from an action, names like <s>Sraṣṭṛ</s>.
In the case of relations such as ownership and lordship, they call the name a name of those who possess that relation.
From the relation of possession come words meaning protector, possessor of wealth, enjoyer, leader, lord, possessor, and so on.
Thus there are forms such as bhūpāla, bhūdhana, bhūbhuj, bhūnetṛ, and bhūpati,
and also bhūmān; this series of examples is to be understood according to poetic convention.
From the sense of producing come equivalent words such as kṛt, kartṛ, sṛṭ, sraṣṭṛ, vidhātṛ, kara, and sū.
So too there are janaka, yonija, ruha, janman, bhū, sūti, aṇa, and the like.
From something borne or held come equivalents such as dhvaja, astra, pāṇi, aṅka, mauli, bhūṣaṇa, and bhṛt.
Words such as śālin, śekhara, forms in the possessive sense, mālin, bhartṛ, and dhara also belong here.
From what is eaten come forms such as bhuj, andha, vrata, liṭ, pāyin, pāśa, aśana, and the like.
From the husband are names like kāntā, priyatamā, vadhū, and praṇayinī.
From the wife or spouse are names like vara, ramaṇa, praṇayin, īśa, and priya.
From friendship comes a term equivalent to sakhi; from something ridden come gāmin, yāna, āsana, and the like.
From kinship come svasṛ, duhitṛ, ātmaja, agraja, avaraja, and similar words.
From an abode or support come terms such as sadman, paryāya, śaya, vāsin, sada, and the like.
From what is to be killed come bhid, dveṣin, jid, ghāti, dhruk, ripu, dhvaṃsin, and śāsana.
Also included are antakārin, damana, darpacchin, mathana, and the like.
For the intended relation, indeed, even from a single word,
the words denoting the relations shown earlier should be joined as appropriate.
For example, when the bull is a mount, one sees the name <s>Vṛṣavāhana</s>.
When ownership is meant, however, there is <s>Vṛṣapati</s>; when bearing a mark is meant, <s>Vṛṣalāñchana</s>.
When a ray is borne, there is <s>Aṃśumālī</s>; when ownership is meant, <s>Aṃśupati</s> or <s>Aṃśumān</s>.
When a snake is the object to be killed, there is <s>Ahiripu</s>; when it is the object eaten, there are <s>Ahibhuk</s> and <s>Śikhī</s>.
By manifest signs even a class-word can become a denoter of an individual.
Thus the southern quarter is called the direction purified by <s>Agasti</s>.
The words ayug and viṣama, meaning odd, denote three, five, seven, and the like.
They should be applied in expressions such as three-eyed, five-arrowed, seven-leaved, and so on.
A quality-word with an opposite meaning, when preceded by nañ or followed by a contrary word,
expresses that opposite; for example, kṛṣṇa can be called asita, non-white, or sitetara, other than white.
In compounds such as vāhya and the like the synonym-substitution appears in the first member; in compounds such as vāḍavāgni it appears in the later member.
In compounds such as bhūbhṛt and similar forms, the replacement by synonyms may occur in both members.
Thus names whose derivation can withstand such inversion are derivational names.
Mixed names, on the other hand, are like gīrvāṇa: they cannot withstand inversion.
The gender to be stated here should be known from the Liṅgānuśāsana.
In the first kāṇḍa are the gods above gods; in the second, the gods.
Humans are in the third; animals are in the fourth, beginning with one-sensed beings.
One-sensed beings are earth, water, fire, air, and trees or plants.
Worms, ants, spiders, and the like are two-, three-, or four-sensed beings.
Five-sensed beings, such as elephants, peacocks, and fish, move on land, in the sky, and in water.

children.text: pañcendriyā eva devā narā nairayikā api ||
children.translated_text: Gods, humans, and hell-beings too are five-sensed.

children.text: nārakāḥ pañcame sāṅgāḥ ṣaṣṭhe sādhāraṇāḥ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Hell-beings are in the fifth section; in the sixth, together with appendices, common terms are plainly set out.
Indeclinables also will be presented here, but particles such as tu, anta, and atha do not precede.
The terms include <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Jina</s>, <s>Pāragata</s>, <s>Trikālavit</s>, <s>Kṣīṇāṣṭakarmā</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, and <s>Adhīśvara</s>.
Also <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Svayambhū</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Jagatprabhu</s>, <s>Tīrthaṃkara</s>, <s>Tīrthakara</s>, and <s>Jineśvara</s>.
Also <s>Syādvādin</s>, <s>Abhayada</s>, <s>Sārva</s>, <s>Sarvajña</s>, <s>Sarvadarśin</s>, and <s>Kevalin</s>.
Also <s>Devādhideva</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, <s>Vītarāga</s>, and <s>Āpta</s>.
In this avasarpiṇī cycle are <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, and <s>Śambhava</s>,
<s>Abhinandana</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, and then the one named <s>Padmaprabha</s>.
Then <s>Supārśva</s>, <s>Candraprabha</s>, <s>Suvidhi</s>, and thereafter <s>Śītala</s>.
<s>Śreyāṃsa</s>, <s>Vāsupūjya</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, and <s>Ananta</s>, the Tīrthakṛt.
<s>Dharma</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Kunthu</s>, <s>Ara</s>, <s>Malli</s>, and <s>Munisuvrata</s>.
<s>Nami</s>, <s>Nemi</s>, <s>Pārśva</s>, and <s>Vīra</s> are the twenty-four Arhats.
<s>Ṛṣabha</s> is also <s>Vṛṣabha</s>; <s>Śreyān</s> is <s>Śreyāṃsa</s>; <s>Anantajit</s> is <s>Ananta</s>.
<s>Suvidhi</s> is <s>Puṣpadanta</s>; <s>Munisuvrata</s> and <s>Suvrata</s> are equivalent.
<s>Ariṣṭanemi</s> is <s>Nemi</s>; <s>Vīra</s> is the last Tīrthakṛt.
He is also <s>Mahāvīra</s>, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, <s>Devārya</s>, and <s>Jñātanandana</s>.
His gaṇas, communities of sages, are nine; the heads of the gaṇas are eleven.
They are <s>Indrabhūti</s>, <s>Agnibhūti</s>, and <s>Vāyubhūti</s>, the <s>Gautamas</s>,
<s>Vyakta</s>, <s>Sudharmā</s>, <s>Maṇḍita</s>, <s>Mauryaputra</s>, and <s>Akampita</s>,
<s>Acalabhrātā</s>, <s>Metārya</s>, and <s>Prabhāsa</s>, each from a distinct family.
The last Kevalin was <s>Jambūsvāmin</s>; then came the lord <s>Prabhava</s>,
<s>Śayyaṃbhava</s>, <s>Yaśobhadra</s>, and then <s>Saṃbhūtavijaya</s>.
<s>Bhadrabāhu</s> and <s>Sthūlabhadra</s> are the six Śrutakevalins.
<s>Mahāgiri</s>, <s>Suhastin</s>, and others ending with <s>Vajra</s> are the Daśapūrvin teachers.
Twenty-two of the Arhats were born in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage.
But <s>Munisuvrata</s> and <s>Nemi</s> were born in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>.
Their fathers are <s>Nābhi</s>, <s>Jitaśatru</s>, <s>Jitāri</s>, and then <s>Saṃvara</s>,
<s>Megha</s>, <s>Dhara</s>, <s>Pratiṣṭha</s>, and King <s>Mahāsena</s>,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and King <s>Vasupūjya</s>,
<s>Kṛtavarmā</s>, <s>Siṃhasena</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, and King <s>Viśvasena</s>,
<s>Sūra</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Kumbha</s>, <s>Sumitra</s>, and <s>Vijaya</s>,
as well as <s>Samudravijaya</s>, <s>Aśvasena</s>, and <s>Siddhārtha</s>.

children.text: marudevā vijayā senā siddhārthā ca maṅgalā
children.translated_text: <s>Marudevā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Senā</s>, <s>Siddhārthā</s>, and <s>Maṅgalā</s> begin the corresponding list of mothers.

children.text: tataḥ susīmā pṛthvī lakṣmaṇā rāmā tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Susīmā</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and after that <s>Rāmā</s>.
<s>Nandā</s>, <s>Viṣṇurjayā</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Suyaśā</s>, <s>Suvratā</s>, and <s>Acirā</s>;

children.text: śrīrdevī prabhāvatī ca padmā vaprā śivā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdevī</s>, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Vaprā</s>, and <s>Śivā</s> as well;
<s>Vāmā</s> and <s>Triśalā</s>: in sequence these are the fathers and mothers of the <s>Arhats</s>.
<s>Gomukha</s>, <s>Mahāyakṣa</s>, <s>Trimukha</s>, and the Yakṣa leader <s>Yakṣanāyaka</s>;
<s>Tumburu</s>, <s>Kusuma</s>, <s>Mātaṅga</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, and <s>Ajita</s>;
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Yakṣeṭ</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, <s>Pātāla</s>, and <s>Kiṃnara</s>;

children.text: garuḍo gandharvo yakṣeṭ kubero varuṇo 'pi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Yakṣeṭ</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> as well;
<s>Bhṛkuṭi</s>, <s>Gomedha</s>, <s>Pārśva</s>, and <s>Mātaṅga</s> are the attendant devotees of the <s>Arhats</s>.
<s>Cakreśvarī</s>, <s>Ajitabalā</s>, <s>Duritāri</s>, and <s>Kālikā</s>;
<s>Mahākālī</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Śāntā</s>, <s>Bhṛkuṭi</s>, and <s>Sutārakā</s>;

children.text: aśokā mānavī caṇḍā viditā cāṅkuśā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Aśokā</s>, <s>Mānavī</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Viditā</s>, and <s>Aṅkuśā</s> as well;
<s>Kandarpā</s>, <s>Nirvāṇī</s>, <s>Balā</s>, <s>Dhāriṇī</s>, and <s>Dharaṇapriyā</s>;
then <s>Naradattā</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, and <s>Padmāvatī</s> as well;
and <s>Siddhāyikā</s>: these are, in order, the Jain <s>śāsana-devatās</s> (attendant deities).

children.text: vṛṣo gajo 'śvaḥ plavagaḥ krauñco 'bjaṃ svastikaḥ śaśī
children.translated_text: The bull, elephant, horse, monkey, curlew, lotus, svastika, and moon;
the <s>makara</s> (sea-creature), <s>śrīvatsa</s> mark, rhinoceros, buffalo, and boar as well;

children.text: śyeno vajraṃ mṛgaśchāgo nandyāvarto ghaṭo 'pi ca
children.translated_text: the falcon, thunderbolt, deer, goat, <s>nandyāvarta</s> symbol, and pitcher too;

children.text: kūrmo nīlotpalaṃ śaṅkhaḥ phaṇī siṃho 'rhatāṃ dhvajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the tortoise, blue lotus, conch, serpent, and lion are the emblems of the <s>Arhats</s>.

children.text: raktau ca padmaprabhavāsupūjyau śuklau tu candraprabhapuṣpadantau
children.translated_text: <s>Padmaprabha</s> and <s>Vāsupūjya</s> are red; <s>Candraprabha</s> and <s>Puṣpadanta</s> are white;
<s>Nemi</s> and <s>Muni</s> are black, <s>Mallī</s> and <s>Pārśva</s> dark blue, and the others have a golden sheen.
In the past <s>utsarpiṇī</s> (ascending cycle) there were twenty-four <s>Arhats</s>:
<s>Kevalajñānī</s>, <s>Nirvāṇī</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, then <s>Mahāyaśas</s>;
<s>Vimala</s>, <s>Sarvānubhūti</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, and <s>Dattatīrthakṛt</s>;
<s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Sutejas</s>, and then <s>Svāmin</s> and <s>Munisuvrata</s>;
<s>Sumati</s>, <s>Śivagati</s>, then <s>Atyāga</s> and <s>Nimīśvara</s>;
<s>Anila</s>, the one called <s>Yaśodhara</s>, then <s>Kṛtārtha</s> and <s>Jineśvara</s>;
<s>Śuddhamati</s>, <s>Śivakara</s>, <s>Syandana</s>, and then <s>Saṃprati</s>.
In the future cycle, however, there will be <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Śūradeva</s>, and <s>Supārśvaka</s>;
<s>Svayaṃprabha</s>, <s>Sarvānubhūti</s>, <s>Devaśruta</s>, and <s>Udaya</s>;
<s>Peḍhāla</s>, <s>Poṭṭila</s>, and also <s>Śatakīrti</s> and <s>Suvrata</s>;
<s>Amama</s>, <s>Niṣkaṣāya</s>, <s>Niṣpulāka</s>, and then <s>Nirmama</s>;
<s>Citragupta</s>, <s>Samādhi</s>, <s>Saṃvara</s>, and <s>Yaśodhara</s>;
<s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Malla</s> and <s>Deva</s>, <s>Anantavīrya</s>, and <s>Bhadrakṛt</s>.
Thus, in all descending and ascending cycles, these are the supreme <s>Jinas</s>.
Their body has wondrous form and fragrance, is free from disease, and is without sweat and dirt;
their breath has the fragrance of a lotus, while their blood and flesh are pure, white as streams of cow's milk and not fetid;
their taking of food and excretion are invisible: these four excellences arise with them.
Even in a field only one <s>yojana</s> across, there is the presence of crores upon crores of humans, gods, and animals;
their speech accords with the languages of humans, animals, gods, and worldly beings, and travels for a <s>yojana</s>;
and a beautiful halo behind the head rivals the splendor of the sun's orb.
For a little more than two hundred <s>gavyūtis</s>, disease, enmity, plague, excessive rain, and drought;
famine and fear from enemy, allied, or one's own armies do not occur: these eleven are born from the destruction of karmas.

children.text: khe dharmacakraṃ camarāḥ sapādapīṭhaṃ mṛgendrāsanamujjvalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: In the sky are the wheel of dharma, fly-whisks, a footstool, and a bright lion-throne;
three umbrellas, a jewel-made banner, and golden lotuses where the feet are placed;
three ramparts, a lovely four-faced manifestation, a <s>caitya</s> tree, and thorns pointing downward;
trees bowing down, the loud sound of drums, a favorable wind, and auspicious birds circling to the right;
rain of scented water, a shower of many-colored flowers, and non-growth of hair, beard, and nails;
and crores of the fourfold human community are present near him, even in a region of the lowest condition;
religious acts and the objects of the senses are favorable: these are
the nineteen divine excellences, and together they make thirty-four.
Refinement, nobility, and being surrounded by courteous expression;
depth like the rumbling of clouds and the ability to produce an answering echo;
rightness, the bringing near of delight, and great meaningfulness;
unobstructedness, cultivated propriety, and the non-arising of doubts;
freedom from being overthrown by another answer, and also penetration into the heart;
mutual expectancy, suitability to the occasion, and steadiness in truth;
not being scattered or prolix, and absence of self-praise and blame of others;
nobility, great smoothness and sweetness, and praiseworthiness;
generosity that does not wound tender spots, and connection with dharma and artha;
no inversion of grammatical case-relations and the like, and freedom from confusion and the like;
variegated artistry, wondrousness, and likewise not being too slow;
variety among many classes and the addition of special distinctions;
predominance of substance, and distinctness of phonemes, words, and sentences;
continuity and tirelessness: these are the thirty-five qualities of speech.
Obstructions relating to giving, gain, power, enjoyment, and repeated enjoyment;

children.text: hāso ratyaratī bhītirjugupsā śoka eva ca ||
children.translated_text: laughter, liking, dislike, fear, disgust, and grief;
desire, false belief, ignorance, sleep, and non-restraint;
disease and hatred: all these eighteen defects do not belong to them.
Great bliss, deathlessness, accomplishment, <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), and non-rebirth;

children.text: śivaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ śreyo nirvāṇaṃ brahma nirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>śiva</s> (blessedness), <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (final good), welfare, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>brahman</s>, and <s>nirvṛti</s> (release);
great arising, the destruction of all suffering, <s>niryāṇa</s> (final departure), and the imperishable are further names for liberation.
Mukti, mokṣa, and apavarga denote liberation; a mumukṣu is one who seeks liberation, a śramaṇa, or a yati.
He is also called a vācaṃyama, a vratin, a sādhu, an anagāra, an ṛṣi, and a muni.
He is a nirgrantha and a bhikṣu; what is proper to him is austerity, yoga, tranquility, and the like.
Yoga, the means to liberation, is constituted by knowledge, faith, and conduct.
Abstaining from speech is mauna; a guru is an instructor in dharma.
The maker of scriptural exposition is an ācārya, while an upādhyāya is a reciter or teacher.
One who has studied the teaching together with its ancillary parts is an anūcāna, and he is also a gaṇin.
A pupil is called śiṣya, vineya, antevāsin, śaikṣa, and prāthamakalpika.
Satīrthyas are those who have the same guru; viveka is distinct individuality or separateness.
Those who mutually practise the same vow of brahmacarya are sabrahmacārins.
Pāramparya, āmnāya, saṃpradāya, and gurukrama all denote tradition or succession through teachers.
The taking of vows is parivrajyā; tapasyā is steadfastness in religious restraints.
The yamas are non-violence, truthful speech, non-stealing, chastity, and non-possession.
The niyamas are purity, contentment, self-study, and austerity.
Devotion to a deity is also included; karaṇa, again, is āsana, bodily posture.
Prāṇāyāma, or prāṇayama, is the restraint of inhalation and exhalation.
Pratyāhāra is the withdrawal of the senses from their objects.
Dhāraṇā is the steady binding of the mind to some chosen object of meditation.
Dhyāna is an uninterrupted continuity of a single cognition concerning that same object.
Samādhi is the condition in which that object alone appears as the content.
Thus yoga is accepted as eightfold, with the eight limbs beginning with yama.
Śvaḥśreyasa, śubha, śiva, kalyāṇa, śvovasīyasa, and śreyas denote good fortune or auspicious welfare.
Kṣema, bhāvuka, bhavika, kuśala, maṅgala, bhadra, madra, and śasta are likewise terms for welfare and auspiciousness.
Svarga, heaven, is also called triviṣṭapa, dyu or div, nāka, and related celestial terms.
It is also gauḥ, tridiva, ūrdhvaloka, and surālaya; those who dwell in that realm are the amaras, the immortals.
The gods are called devas, suparvans, suras, nirjaras, devatās, ṛbhus, barhirmukhas, animiṣas, daivatas, and nākilekhas.
They are also vṛndārakas, sumanases, tridaśas, amartyas, eaters of svāhā, svadhā, sacrifice, and nectar, and the Āditeyas.
They are gīrvāṇas, <s>Maruts</s>, sleepless ones, vibudhas, and enemies of the <s>Dānavas</s>.
Their vehicle is a vimāna; their drink is andhas, pīyūṣa, amṛta, or sudhā, nectar.
The <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Taḍits</s>, <s>Suparṇakas</s>, <s>Vahnis</s>, <s>Anilas</s>, and <s>Stanitas</s>,
together with the <s>Udadhi</s>, <s>Dvīpa</s>, and <s>Diś</s> classes, are the ten lords of dwellings, ending with the <s>Kumāras</s>.

children.text: syuḥ piśācā bhūtā yakṣā rākṣasāḥ kiṃnarā api
children.translated_text: The <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>,
and the <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s> are these intermediate beings.
The jyotiṣkas, the luminous beings, are five: the moon, the sun, the planets, the lunar mansions, and the stars.

children.text: vaimānikāḥ punaḥ kalpabhavā dvādaśa te tvamī ||
children.translated_text: The vaimānikas, again, are the gods born in the kalpas; these are twelve.
They are those born in <s>Saudharma</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Māhendra</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, and <s>Lāntaka</s>,
and those born in <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Sahasrāra</s>, <s>Ānata</s>, <s>Prāṇata</s>, <s>Āraṇa</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s>.
Beyond the kalpas are the nine <s>Graiveyakas</s> and the five <s>Anuttaras</s>.
Thus, according to the division of classes, the gods are said to be fourfold.

children.text: ādityaḥ savitāryamā kharasahasroṣṇāṃśur aṃśū ravirmārtaṇḍastaraṇirgabhastiraruṇo bhānurnabho 'harmaṇiḥ
children.translated_text: The sun is called <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, Kharasahasra, Uṣṇāṃśu, Aṃśu, <s>Ravi</s>, <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, Taraṇi, Gabhasti, <s>Aruṇa</s>, Bhānu, Nabhas, and Aharmaṇi.

children.text: sūryo 'rkaḥ kiraṇo bhago grahapuṣaḥ pūṣā pataṅgaḥ khago mārtāṇḍo yamunākṛtāntajanakaḥ pradyotanastāpanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Arka</s>, Kiraṇa, <s>Bhaga</s>, Grahapuṣ, <s>Pūṣan</s>, Pataṅga, Khaga, <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s>, father of <s>Yamunā</s> and <s>Kṛtānta</s>, Pradyotana, and Tāpana.
It is Bradhna, Haṃsa, Citrabhānu, <s>Vivasvān</s>, Sūra, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, Dvādaśātman, and Heli.
It is <s>Mitra</s>, enemy of darkness, lotus-rayed-handed, friend of the day-lotus, and Saptasapti, the seven-horsed one.
Day is divā, dina, ahar, and divasa; light is prabhā, vibhā, bhā, and bhāsa; kara is a ray, and <s>Mihira</s> and <s>Virocana</s> are names of the sun.
The lord of planets, lotuses, cows, and the sky is also <s>Vikartana</s>, <s>Hari</s>, Śuci, and the traveller born in the sky and the day.
It is Haridaśva, witness of the world's deeds, Bhāsvat, and Vibhāvasu.
It is the embodiment of the three Vedas, the eye of the world, Tapana, and Aruṇasārathi, whose charioteer is <s>Aruṇa</s>.
Rociḥ, usra, ruci, śocis, aṃśu, go, jyotis, arciḥ, upadhṛti, and abhīśu are terms for ray and radiance.
Pragraha, śuci, marīci, dīpti, dhāman, ketu, ghṛṇi, raśmi, and pṛśni are likewise rays or lights.
Pāda, dīdhiti, kara, dyuti, dyot, ruc, viroka, kiraṇa, tviṣit, and tviṣ also denote brightness or rays.
Bhā, prabhā, vasu, gabhasti, bhānu, bhā, mayūkha, mahas, chavi, and vibhā are further words for light and radiance.
Prakāśa, tejas, uddyota, āloka, varcas, and ātapa mean brightness, brilliance, light, or heat.
Marīcikā is a mirage or mṛgatṛṣṇā; maṇḍala is the sun's disk or a mock sun.
Paridhi and pariveṣa denote a halo; the sun's charioteer is <s>Kāśyapi</s>.
He is <s>Anūru</s>, son of <s>Vinatā</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, and elder brother of <s>Garuḍa</s>.
<s>Revanta</s>, born from the sun's seed, is Plavaga and Hayavāhana, the horse-mounted one.
The eighteen beginning with <s>Māṭhara</s> are the attendants standing around <s>Savitṛ</s>, the sun.
The moon is <s>Candramas</s>, friend of the water-lily, one with ten white horses, source of nectar, and lord of the lunar days.
It is lord of moonlight, of the night-blooming lilies, of the hare-mark, of <s>Rohiṇī</s>, of brahmins, of night, and of medicinal herbs.
It is <s>Jaivātṛka</s>, Abja, Kalāśa, Śaiṇa, Chāyābhṛt, <s>Indu</s>, <s>Vidhu</s>, and the one born from <s>Atri</s>'s eye.

children.text: rājā niśo ratnakarau ca candraḥ somo 'mṛtaśvetahimadyutir glauḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is king of the night and of jewel-mines; it is <s>Candra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, Amṛta, Śveta, Himadyuti, and Glauḥ.

children.text: ṣoḍaśo 'ṃśaḥ kalā cihnaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣma lāñchanam
children.translated_text: A kalā is a sixteenth part; cihna, lakṣaṇa, lakṣma, and lāñchana mean a mark or sign.
Aṅka, kalaṅka, and abhijñāna also mean a mark; candrikā and candragolikā denote moonlight or a moonbeam.

children.text: candrātapaḥ kaumudī ca jyotsnā bimbaṃ tu maṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Candrātapa, kaumudī, and jyotsnā are moonlight; bimba and maṇḍala are the disk.
Nakṣatra, tārakā, tārā, jyotis, bha, uḍu, and graha denote a star or luminary.
Dhiṣṇya and ṛkṣa also mean a lunar mansion; <s>Aśvinī</s> is <s>Aśvakinī</s>, with the <s>Dasras</s> as its deities.
It is also <s>Aśvayuj</s> and <s>Vālinī</s>; next, <s>Bharaṇī</s> has <s>Yama</s> as its deity.
<s>Kṛttikā</s> is also called the <s>Bahulās</s> and has <s>Agni</s> as its deity; <s>Rohiṇī</s> is Brāhmī.
<s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s> is also <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Mārga</s>, Cāndramasa, and <s>Mṛga</s>.
The <s>Ilvalās</s>, or <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, are the five stars situated in the head.

children.text: ārdrā tu kālinī raudrī punarvasū tu yāmakau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ārdrā</s> is <s>Kālinī</s> and <s>Raudrī</s>; the <s>Punarvasūs</s> are the <s>Yāmakas</s>.
They are also the two <s>Ādityas</s>; <s>Puṣpa</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, and <s>Sidhya</s> have <s>Guru</s> as their deity.
<s>Aśleṣā</s> is serpent-deitied; <s>Maghā</s> is ancestral; <s>Phālgunī</s> has <s>Yoni</s> as deity.
That same one, as <s>Uttarā</s>, has <s>Aryaman</s> as deity; <s>Hasta</s> has <s>Savitṛ</s> as deity.
<s>Citrā</s> is <s>Tvāṣṭrī</s>; <s>Svāti</s> is <s>Ānilī</s>; the <s>Viśākhās</s> have <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> as deities.

children.text: rādhānurādhā tu maitrī jyeṣṭhaindrī mūla āsrapaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anurādhā</s> is <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Maitrī</s>; <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is <s>Aindrī</s>; <s>Mūla</s> is <s>Āsrapa</s>.

children.text: pūrvāṣāḍhā tu sottarā syādvaiśvī śravaṇaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, together with <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, is <s>Vaiśvī</s>; <s>Śravaṇa</s>, again, is...
deitied by <s>Hari</s>; <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, or <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, has the <s>Vasus</s> as deities.
<s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> is <s>Vāruṇī</s>; the following ones have <s>Aja</s> and <s>Ahirbudhna</s> as deities.
They are the former and latter <s>Bhādrapadās</s>, also called <s>Dṛśyas</s> and <s>Proṣṭhapadās</s>.

children.text: revatī tu pauṣṇaṃ dākṣāyaṇyaḥ sarvāḥ śaśipriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s> is <s>Pauṣṇī</s>; all the <s>Dākṣāyaṇīs</s> are dear to the moon.
The rising of the zodiac signs is the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant); those signs begin with <s>Meṣa</s>.
<s>Āra</s>, <s>Vakra</s>, <s>Lohitāṅga</s>, <s>Maṅgala</s>, <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, and <s>Kuja</s> are names of Mars.
<s>Āṣāḍhābhū</s>, <s>Navārci</s>, <s>Budha</s>, <s>Saumya</s>, and <s>Praharṣula</s> are names of Mercury.
<s>Jña</s>, <s>Pañcārci</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhābhū</s>, <s>Śyāmāṅga</s>, and <s>Rohiṇīsuta</s> are also names of Mercury.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Surācārya</s>, <s>Jīva</s>, and <s>Citraśikhaṇḍija</s> are names of Jupiter.
<s>Vācaspati</s>, <s>Dvādaśārci</s>, <s>Dhiṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Phālgunībhava</s> are also names of Jupiter.
<s>Gīrbṛhatyoḥpati</s>, <s>Utathyānuja</s>, <s>Aṅgirasa</s>, and <s>Guru</s> are further names of Jupiter.

children.text: śukro maghābhavaḥ kāvya uśanā bhārgavaḥ kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Maghābhava</s>, <s>Kāvya</s>, <s>Uśanā</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, and <s>Kavi</s> are names of Venus.
<s>Ṣoḍaśārci</s>, <s>Daityaguru</s>, and <s>Dhiṣṇya</s> are also Venus; <s>Śanaiścara</s> and <s>Śani</s> are Saturn.
<s>Chāyāsuta</s>, <s>Asita</s>, <s>Sauri</s>, <s>Saptārci</s>, and <s>Revatībhava</s> are also names of Saturn.
<s>Manda</s>, <s>Kroḍa</s>, and <s>Nīlavāsas</s> are further names of Saturn; <s>Svarbhāṇu</s>, however, is <s>Vidhuṃtuda</s>.
<s>Tamas</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Saiṃhikeya</s>, and <s>Bharaṇībhū</s> are names of Rāhu; then <s>Ahika</s>...
<s>Aśleṣābhū</s>, <s>Śikhī</s>, and <s>Ketu</s> are names of Ketu; <s>Dhruva</s> is the son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>.
<s>Agastya</s>, <s>Agasti</s>, <s>Pītābdhi</s>, <s>Vātāpidviṣ</s>, and <s>Ghaṭodbhava</s> are names of <s>Agastya</s>.
<s>Maitrāvaruṇi</s>, <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Aurvaśeya</s>, and <s>Agnimāruta</s> are also names of <s>Agastya</s>.
<s>Lopāmudrā</s>, his wife, is also <s>Kauṣītakī</s> and <s>Varapradā</s>.
The seven seers beginning with <s>Marīci</s> are called <s>Citraśikhaṇḍins</s>.
In a single expression, the moon and the sun are called <s>Puṣpadantau</s> and <s>Puṣpavantau</s>.
The seizure of the sun or moon by <s>Rāhu</s> is an eclipse, called <s>graha</s>, <s>uparāga</s>, or <s>upaplava</s>.
A bad sign is <s>upaliṅga</s> or <s>ariṣṭa</s>; an affliction is <s>upasarga</s> or <s>upadrava</s>.
<s>Ajanya</s>, <s>īti</s>, <s>utpāta</s>, <s>vahnyutpāta</s>, and <s>upāhita</s> denote calamities or portents.
Time is called <s>kāla</s>, <s>samaya</s>, <s>diṣṭa</s>, <s>anehas</s>, and <s>sarvabhūṣaka</s>.
Time is twofold by the distinction between <s>avasarpiṇī</s> (descending cycle) and <s>utsarpiṇī</s> (ascending cycle).
That cycle is completed in twenty crore-crores of <s>sāgaras</s>.

children.text: avasarpiṇyāṃ ṣaḍarā utsarpiṇyāṃ ta eva viparītāḥ
children.translated_text: In an <s>avasarpiṇī</s> there are six eras; in an <s>utsarpiṇī</s> those same eras occur in reverse.
Thus this wheel of time turns through twelve eras.
Among them, the <s>ekāntasuṣamā</s> era lasts four crore-crores
of <s>sāgaras</s>; the <s>suṣamā</s> era lasts three crore-crores.
The <s>suṣamaduḥṣamā</s> era lasts two; the <s>duḥṣamasuṣamā</s> era, in turn,
lasts one crore-crore, less by forty-two thousand years.
Then the <s>duḥṣamā</s> era is twenty-one thousand years, and the same amount
belongs also to <s>ekāntaduḥṣamā</s>; the remaining eras have these numbers in reverse.
In the first three eras, mortals live for three, two, and one <s>palya</s>, respectively.
Their height is three, two, and one <s>gavyūti</s>, and they eat after three, two, and one days.
They are satisfied with the fruit of wish-fulfilling trees; but in the fourth era people
live for a crore of <s>pūrvas</s> and are five hundred bows in height.
In the fifth era, however, people live for a hundred years and are seven hands in height.
In the sixth, again, they live for sixteen years and are one cubit in height.
They are filled with utter misery; in the <s>utsarpiṇī</s> too such conditions
are to be understood in reverse order through all six eras.
Eighteen <s>nimeṣas</s> make a <s>kāṣṭhā</s>; two <s>kāṣṭhās</s> make a <s>lava</s>.
Fifteen of those make a <s>kalā</s>, and two of that make a <s>leśa</s>.
Fifteen of those make a <s>kṣaṇa</s>; six <s>kṣaṇas</s> make a <s>nāḍikā</s>.

children.text: sā dhārikā ca ghaṭikā muhūrtastaddvayena ca ||
children.translated_text: That is also called <s>dhārikā</s> and <s>ghaṭikā</s>; two of those make a <s>muhūrta</s>.
Thirty of these make a day-and-night; within that, the day is <s>ahar</s>, <s>divasa</s>, or <s>dina</s>.

children.text: divaṃ dyur vāsaro ghasraḥ prabhātaṃ syādaharmukham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Div</s>, <s>dyu</s>, <s>vāsara</s>, and <s>ghasra</s> are also day; dawn is <s>prabhāta</s> or <s>aharmukha</s>.
Dawn is also <s>vyuṣṭa</s>, <s>vibhāta</s>, <s>pratyūṣa</s>, <s>kalya</s>, <s>pratyuṣas</s>, and <s>uṣas</s>.

children.text: kālyaṃ madhyāhnastu divāmadhyaṃ madhyaṃdinaṃ ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Morning is <s>kālya</s>; midday is the middle of the day, <s>madhyaṃdina</s>.
The end of the day is <s>dināvasāna</s>, <s>utsūra</s>, <s>vikāla</s>, or <s>sabalī</s>.
Evening is <s>sāyam</s>, <s>saṃdhyā</s>, or <s>pitṛsū</s>; <s>trisaṃdhya</s> is also <s>upavaiṇava</s>.
<s>Kutapa</s> is the time for a <s>śrāddha</s>, the eighth portion of the day.

children.text: niśā niśīthinī rātriḥ śarvarī kṣaṇadā kṣapā ||
children.translated_text: Night is <s>niśā</s>, <s>niśīthinī</s>, <s>rātri</s>, <s>śarvarī</s>, <s>kṣaṇadā</s>, and <s>kṣapā</s>.

children.text: triyāmā yāminī bhautī tamī tamā vibhāvarī
children.translated_text: It is also <s>triyāmā</s>, <s>yāminī</s>, <s>bhautī</s>, <s>tamī</s>, <s>tamā</s>, and <s>vibhāvarī</s>.
It is also <s>rajanī</s>, <s>vasati</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>vāsateyī</s>, and <s>tamasvinī</s>.
It is <s>uṣā</s>, <s>doṣā</s>, and <s>indukāntā</s>; <s>tamisrā</s> is the new-moon night.
<s>Jyautsnī</s> is the full-moon night; a group of nights is <s>gaṇarātra</s> or <s>niśāgaṇa</s>.
A <s>pakṣiṇī</s> is a night enclosed by two days equal to a fortnight.
<s>Garbhaka</s> is a pair of nights; <s>pradoṣa</s> is the beginning of night.
<s>Yāma</s> and <s>prahara</s> are a watch; <s>niśītha</s>, <s>ardharātra</s>, and <s>mahāniśā</s> are midnight.
<s>Uccandra</s> is the latter part of night; darkness is <s>tamisra</s>, <s>timira</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.
Darkness is also <s>dhvānta</s>, <s>bhūchāyā</s>, <s>andhakāra</s>, <s>tamasa</s>, and <s>samavāndhata</s>.
At the time when night and day are equal, that is <s>viṣuvat</s> or <s>viṣuva</s>.
A <s>pakṣa</s> is fifteen days and nights; the dark fortnight is <s>bahula</s> or <s>asita</s>.
A lunar day is <s>tithi</s> or <s>karmavāṭī</s>; <s>pratipad</s> and <s>pakṣati</s> are equivalent.
The two fifteenth lunar days are sacrificial times, the ends of fortnights, and <s>parvaṇs</s>.
The interval between <s>Bhūteṣṭā</s> and the fifteenth lunar day is <s>parvamūla</s>.
The interval between the first and fifteenth lunar days is the <s>parvasaṃdhi</s>, the junction of a sacred division.

children.text: pūrṇimā paurṇamāsī sā rākā pūrṇe niśākare ||
children.translated_text: When the night-maker, the moon, is full, that day is <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, or <s>Rākā</s>.
When it lacks a digit it is <s>Anumati</s>; the <s>Mārgaśīrṣī</s> full moon is <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s>.
The new moon is <s>Amā</s>, <s>Amāvasyā</s>, <s>Darśa</s>, or the conjunction of sun and moon.

children.text: amāvāsyāmāvāsī ca sā naṣṭenduḥ kuhuḥ kuhūḥ
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Amāvasyā</s>, <s>Amāvāsī</s>, the lost-moon day, <s>Kuhu</s>, or <s>Kuhū</s>.
When the moon is seen it is <s>Sinīvālī</s>; <s>Bhūteṣṭā</s> is the fourteenth lunar day.
A fortnight is <s>pakṣa</s>, a month is <s>māsa</s>; <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, the beginning of the year, is also <s>Saha</s> or <s>Sahā</s>.
It is also <s>Āgrahāyaṇika</s>; next, <s>Pauṣa</s> is <s>Taiṣa</s> and <s>Sahasya</s>.
<s>Māgha</s> is <s>Tapas</s>; <s>Phālguna</s> is <s>Phālgunika</s> and <s>Tapasya</s>.
<s>Caitra</s> is <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Caitrika</s>; for <s>Vaiśākha</s> the names are <s>Rādha</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Jyeṣṭha</s> is <s>Śukra</s>; then <s>Āṣāḍha</s> is <s>Śuci</s>; <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> is <s>Nabhas</s>.
<s>Śrāvaṇa</s> is also <s>Śrāvaṇika</s>; then <s>Bhādrapada</s> is <s>Nabhasya</s>, <s>Proṣṭhabhādra</s>, and <s>Pada</s>.
It is also <s>Bhādra</s>; in <s>Āśvina</s> the names are <s>Āśvayuja</s> and <s>Iṣa</s>; next comes <s>Kārtika</s>.
<s>Kārtika</s> is also <s>Kārtikika</s>, <s>Bāhula</s>, and <s>Ūrja</s>; from <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> onward, each pair of months is a season.
<s>Hemanta</s> is <s>Praśala</s> and <s>Raudra</s>; <s>Śaiṣa</s> and <s>Śiśira</s> are equivalent.
<s>Vasanta</s> is <s>Iṣya</s>, <s>Surabhi</s>, <s>Puṣpakāla</s>, and <s>Balāṅgaka</s>.
The hot season is <s>Uṣṇa</s>, <s>Uṣṇāgama</s>, <s>Grīṣma</s>, <s>Nidāgha</s>, <s>Tapa</s>, and <s>Ūṣmaka</s>.
The rains are <s>Varṣā</s>, <s>Tapātyaya</s>, <s>Prāvṛṣ</s>, <s>Meghakāla</s>, <s>Āgama</s>, and <s>Kṣarī</s>.
<s>Śarad</s>, autumn, is <s>Ghanātyaya</s>; an <s>ayana</s> is made up of two groups of three seasons beginning with <s>Śiśira</s>.
The two <s>ayanas</s> are the northward and southward course of the sun; a complete year is <s>vatsara</s>.

children.text: sa saṃparyanūdbhyo varṣaṃ hāyano 'bdaṃ samāḥ śarat
children.translated_text: The year is also <s>saṃvatsara</s>, <s>parivatsara</s>, <s>anuvatsara</s>, <s>udvatsara</s>, <s>varṣa</s>, <s>hāyana</s>, <s>abda</s>, <s>samā</s>, and <s>śarad</s>.
A month makes a day and night of the ancestors; a year makes one of the gods.

children.text: daive yugasahasre dve brāhmaṃ kalpau tu tau nṛṇām
children.translated_text: In divine reckoning, two thousand <s>yugas</s> make a day and night of <s>Brahmā</s>; for human beings those two are two <s>kalpas</s>.
A <s>manvantara</s> is seventy-one divine <s>yugas</s>.

children.text: kalpo guṇāntaḥ kalpāntaḥ saṃhāraḥ pralayaḥ kṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>kalpa</s> is also <s>guṇānta</s>; the end of a <s>kalpa</s> is <s>saṃhāra</s>, <s>pralaya</s>, or <s>kṣaya</s>.
The same dissolution is <s>saṃvarta</s>, <s>parivarta</s>, <s>samasupti</s>, and <s>jihānaka</s>.
Its time is <s>tadātva</s>; a result born at that time is a <s>sāṃdṛṣṭika</s> fruit, a present and visible result.
<s>Āyati</s> is later time; <s>udarka</s> is a result that arises from that later time.
The sky is called <s>vyoman</s>, <s>antarikṣa</s>, <s>gagana</s>, <s>ghanāśraya</s>, <s>vihāyas</s>, <s>ākāśa</s>, <s>ananta</s>, and <s>puṣkara</s>.

children.text: abhraṃ surābhroḍumarutpatho 'mbaraṃ khaṃ dyodivau viṣṇupadaṃ viyannabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is also <s>abhra</s>, <s>surābhra</s>, the path of stars and wind, <s>ambara</s>, <s>kha</s>, <s>dyo</s>, <s>div</s>, <s>Viṣṇupada</s>, <s>viyat</s>, and <s>nabhas</s>.
Clouds are <s>nabhrāṭ</s>, <s>taḍitvān</s>, <s>mudira</s>, <s>ghanāghana</s>, <s>abhra</s>, <s>dhūmayoni</s>, <s>stanayitnu</s>, and <s>megha</s>.
They are also <s>jīmūta</s>, <s>parjanya</s>, <s>balāhaka</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>dhārādhara</s>, <s>vāhada</s>, <s>ambudhara</s>, and <s>jalada</s>.
A mass of clouds is <s>kādambinī</s> or <s>meghamālā</s>; a gloomy day is darkness born of clouds.
<s>Āsāra</s> is a rushing rainfall; <s>śīkara</s> is water struck or driven by wind.
<s>Vṛṣṭi</s>, <s>varṣaṇa</s>, and <s>varṣa</s> mean rain; <s>grāha</s>, <s>graha</s>, and <s>avavāta</s> mean its obstruction.
<s>Ghanopala</s> or <s>karaka</s> is hail; a direction is <s>kāṣṭhā</s>, <s>āśā</s>, <s>diś</s>, <s>harit</s>, or <s>kakubh</s>.

children.text: pūrvā prācī dakṣiṇāpācī pratīcī tu paścimā
children.translated_text: The east is <s>pūrvā</s> or <s>prācī</s>; the south is <s>dakṣiṇā</s> or <s>apācī</s>; the west is <s>pratīcī</s> or <s>paścimā</s>.
<s>Aparā</s> is also west; the north is <s>uttarā</s> or <s>udīcī</s>; an intermediate direction is <s>vidiś</s>, <s>upadiś</s>, or <s>pradiś</s>.
A thing belonging to a direction is <s>diśya</s> or <s>digbhava</s>; southern is <s>apāga</s> or <s>apācīna</s>, and northern is <s>udag</s> or <s>udīcīna</s>.
For eastern, <s>prāk</s> and <s>prācīna</s> are equivalent; for western, <s>pratyak</s> and <s>pratīcīna</s> are used.
The lords of the directions, in order, are <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Nairṛta</s>,
<s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s>.
The directional elephants are <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, and <s>Añjana</s>,
and <s>Puṣpadanta</s>, <s>Sārvabhauma</s>, and <s>Supratīka</s>.
<s>Indra</s> is <s>Hari</s>, <s>Duścyavana</s>, <s>Acyutāgraja</s>, <s>Vajrī</s>, <s>Viḍaujā</s>, <s>Maghavān</s>, and <s>Puraṃdara</s>.
He is <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, <s>Puruhūta</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Saṃkrandana</s>, <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, and <s>Meghavāhana</s>.
He is <s>Sutrāman</s>, <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, <s>Dalmi</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Vṛṣan</s>, <s>Śunāsīra</s>, and <s>Sahasranetra</s>.
He is <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Haryaśva</s>, <s>Ṛbhukṣin</s>, <s>Bāhudanteya</s>, <s>Vṛddhaśravas</s>, and <s>Turāṣāṭ</s>.
He is <s>Surarṣabha</s>, <s>Tapastakṣa</s>, <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, <s>Vara</s>, and <s>Śatakratu</s>.
He is <s>Kauśika</s>, lord of the eastern direction, lord of the gods, lord of the apsarases, lord of heaven, and lord of <s>Śacī</s>.
He is <s>Pṛtanāṣāṭ</s>, <s>Ugradhanvan</s>, <s>Marutvān</s>, and <s>Maghavān</s>; his foes are...
His foes are <s>Pāka</s>, the mountains, <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Puloman</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, and <s>Bala</s>.
<s>Jambha</s> is another; his beloved wife is <s>Śacī</s>, <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Paulomī</s>, or <s>Jayavāhinī</s>.
His son is <s>Jayanta</s>, also called <s>Jayadatta</s> and <s>Jaya</s>.
His daughter is <s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Tavīṣī</s>, or <s>Tāviṣī</s>; his horse is <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>.
His charioteer is <s>Mātali</s>; his gatekeeper is <s>Devanandī</s>; his elephant, again, is...
<s>Airāvaṇa</s>, <s>Abhramātaṅga</s>, <s>Caturdanta</s>, and <s>Arkasodara</s>,
or <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Hastimalla</s>, <s>Śvetagaja</s>, and <s>Abhramupriya</s>.
His palace and banner are both <s>Vaijayanta</s>; his city is <s>Amarāvatī</s>.
His lake is <s>Nandīsara</s>; his assembly hall is <s>Sudharmā</s>; his garden is <s>Nandana</s>.
His tree is the <s>Kalpa</s> tree, <s>Pārijāta</s>, <s>Mandāra</s>, or <s>Haricandana</s>;
it is also <s>Saṃtāna</s>; his bow is <s>Devāyudha</s>, and when straight it is <s>Rohita</s>.
When long and straight it is <s>Airāvata</s>; the thunderbolt is <s>Vajra</s>, <s>Aśani</s>, <s>Hrādinī</s>, or <s>Svaru</s>.
It is also <s>Śatakoṭi</s>, <s>Pavi</s>, <s>Śamba</s>, <s>Dambholi</s>, <s>Bhidura</s>, and <s>Bhidu</s>.
It is <s>Vyādhāma</s> and <s>Kuliśa</s>; its flash is <s>Atibhī</s>, and its sound is <s>Sphūrjathu</s>.
The heavenly physicians are the two <s>Aśvins</s>, sons of <s>Aśvinī</s>, sons of <s>Vaḍavā</s>.
The pair are also <s>Nāsikya</s>, sons of <s>Arka</s>, <s>Dasra</s>, <s>Nāsatya</s>, ocean-born, and the twin pair.
<s>Viśvakarman</s> is also <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Viśvakṛt</s>, and the divine carpenter.
The apsarases are the wives of heaven-dwellers, the courtesans of heaven, headed by <s>Urvaśī</s>.
<s>Hāhā</s> and the others are <s>Gandharvas</s>, heavenly musicians.
<s>Yama</s> is <s>Kṛtānta</s>, lord of the ancestors, lord of the southern quarter, lord of departed beings, staff-bearer, and son of <s>Arka</s>.
He is <s>Kīnāśa</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, <s>Samavartin</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Śīrṇāṅgihari</s>, <s>Antaka</s>, and <s>Dharmarāja</s>.
<s>Yamarāja</s>, <s>Śrāddhadeva</s>, <s>Śamana</s>, and <s>Mahiṣadhvaja</s> are names of <s>Yama</s>;
and so is <s>Kālindīsodara</s>; <s>Dhūmorṇā</s> is his beloved wife.
His city is <s>Saṃyamanī</s>, and his doorkeeper is <s>Vaidhyata</s>;
his two servants are <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Mahācaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Citragupta</s> is his scribe.
<s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Puṇyajana</s>, <s>Nṛcakṣas</s>, <s>Yātvāśara</s>, <s>Kauṇapa</s>, and <s>Yātudhāna</s> are terms for a demon;
<s>Rātriṃcara</s>, <s>Rātricara</s>, <s>Palāda</s>, <s>Kīnāśa</s>, <s>Rakṣas</s>, and <s>Nikasātmaja</s> are also such names.
<s>Kavyāt</s>, <s>Karbura</s>, <s>Nairṛta</s>, and <s>Asṛkpa</s> are further demon-names; <s>Varuṇa</s> is called <s>Arṇavamandira</s> and <s>Pracetā</s>;
also <s>Jalayādaspati</s>, <s>Pāśin</s>, <s>Meghanāda</s>, <s>Jalakāntāra</s>, and <s>Paraṃjana</s>.
<s>Śrīda</s>, <s>Sitodara</s>, <s>Kuheśasakha</s>, <s>Piśācakīchāvasu</s>, <s>Triśiras</s>, <s>Ailabila</s>, and <s>Ekapinga</s>,
<s>Paulastya</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Ratnakara</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Nṛdharma</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, and <s>Naravāhana</s> are names of <s>Kubera</s>.
He is <s>Kailāsaukas</s>, <s>Yakṣadhananidhi</s>, and <s>Kiṃpuruṣeśvara</s>;

children.text: vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ caitrarathaṃ vanaṃ purī prabhā ||
children.translated_text: his aerial car is <s>Puṣpaka</s>, his grove is <s>Caitraratha</s>, and his city is <s>Prabhā</s>.
<s>Alakā</s> and <s>Vasvokasārā</s> are also names of his city; his son is <s>Nalakūvara</s>.

children.text: vittaṃ rikthaṃ svāpateyaṃ rāḥ sāraṃ vibhavo vasu ||
children.translated_text: Wealth is called <s>vitta</s>, <s>riktha</s>, <s>svāpateya</s>, <s>rā</s>, <s>sāra</s>, <s>vibhava</s>, and <s>vasu</s>;

children.text: dyumnaṃ dravyaṃ pṛkthamṛkthaṃ svamṛṇaṃ draviṇaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: also <s>dyumna</s>, <s>dravya</s>, <s>pṛktha</s>, <s>ṛktha</s>, <s>sva</s>, <s>mṛṇa</s>, <s>draviṇa</s>, and <s>dhana</s>.
<s>Hiraṇya</s> is a word for wealth or gold; a treasure is <s>nidhāna</s>, <s>kunābhi</s>, <s>śevadhi</s>, or <s>nidhi</s>.
<s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Makara</s>, and <s>Kacchapa</s>,
together with <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Kunda</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Kharva</s>, are the nine treasures.
A <s>yakṣa</s> is also called <s>puṇyajana</s>, <s>rāja</s>, <s>guhyaka</s>, or <s>vaṭavāsin</s>;
a <s>kiṃnara</s> is <s>kiṃpuruṣa</s>, <s>turaṅgavadana</s>, or <s>mayu</s>.

children.text: śaṃbhuḥ śarvaḥ sthāṇurīśāna īśo rudroḍḍīśau vāmadevo vṛṣāṅkaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Uḍḍīśa</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Vṛṣāṅka</s> are names of <s>Śiva</s>;
<s>Kaṇṭhekāla</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Bharga</s> too.
Also <s>Mṛtyuṃjaya</s>, <s>Pañcamukha</s>, <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s>, <s>Śmaśānaveśman</s>, <s>Giriśa</s>, and <s>Girīśa</s>;
<s>Ṣaṇḍha</s>, <s>Kapardī</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Ūrdhvaliṅga</s>, <s>Ekatridṛk</s>, <s>Bhāladṛk</s>, and <s>Ekapāda</s>.
<s>Mṛḍa</s>, <s>Aṭṭahāsin</s>, <s>Ghanavāhana</s>, <s>Ahirbudhna</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and <s>Viṣāntaka</s> are also names;
<s>Mahāvratin</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Hiraṇyaretas</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Asthidhanvan</s>, and <s>Puruṣāsthimālin</s> as well.
<s>Vyomakeśa</s>, <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Dikkṛttivāsas</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, and <s>Nīlalohita</s> are given;
<s>Sarvajña</s>, <s>Nāṭyapriya</s>, <s>Khaṇḍapaśu</s>, <s>Mahāpara</s>, <s>Devanaṭeśvara</s>, and <s>Hara</s> complete this group.
<s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Pramathapati</s>, <s>Bhūtapati</s>, <s>Umāpati</s>, and <s>Piṅgajaṭekṣaṇa</s> are further names of <s>Śiva</s>;
he bears <s>Pināka</s>, the trident, the skull-staff, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a serpent, the moon, and a skull.
He is the foe of <s>Gaja</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Pura</s>, <s>Anaṅga</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Andhaka</s>, and <s>Makha</s>;
<s>Kaparda</s> is his mass of matted hair; <s>Khaṭvāṅga</s> is his skull-staff.
<s>Pināka</s>, <s>Ājagava</s>, and <s>Ajakāva</s> are names of that bow.

children.text: brāhmyādyā mātaraḥ sapta pramathāḥ pārṣadā gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The seven Mothers are <s>Brāhmī</s> and the others; the <s>Pramathas</s>, <s>Pārṣadas</s>, and <s>Gaṇas</s> are his retinue.
The powers are <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>vaśitā</s> (subjugating control), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), <s>prākāmya</s> (unhindered will), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), and <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness);
together with <s>yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> (settling wherever one wishes) and <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), these make the eightfold sovereignty.

children.text: gaurī kālī pārvatī mātṛmātāparṇā rudrāṇyambikā tryambakomā
children.translated_text: Names of the Goddess are <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>, <s>Mātṛmātā</s>, <s>Aparṇā</s>, <s>Rudrāṇī</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Tryambakā</s>, and <s>Umā</s>;

children.text: durgā caṇḍī siṃhayānā mṛḍānīkātyāyanyau dakṣajāryā kumārī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Siṃhayānā</s>, <s>Mṛḍānī</s>, <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, <s>Dakṣajā</s>, <s>Āryā</s>, and <s>Kumārī</s>;
<s>Satī</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Mahādevī</s>, <s>Śarvāṇī</s>, and <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>;
<s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Mainākasvasā</s>, <s>Menādrijā</s>, and <s>Īśvarā</s>.
She is the slayer of <s>Niśumbha</s>, <s>Śumbha</s>, and <s>Mahiṣa</s>, and is <s>Bhūtanāyikā</s>;

children.text: tasyāḥ siṃho manastātnaḥ sakhyau tu vijayā jayā ||
children.translated_text: her lion is <s>Manastātna</s>, and her two friends are <s>Vijayā</s> and <s>Jayā</s>.
Forms or names include <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, <s>Carcikā</s>, <s>Carmamuṇḍā</s>, and <s>Mārjārakarṇikā</s>;
<s>Karṇamoṭī</s>, <s>Mahāgandhā</s>, <s>Bhairavī</s>, and <s>Kapālinī</s>.
<s>Heramba</s>, <s>Gaṇa</s>, <s>Vighneśa</s>, <s>Parśupāṇi</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s> are names of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>;
<s>Dvaimātura</s>, <s>Gajāsya</s>, <s>Ekadanta</s>, <s>Lambodara</s>, and <s>Ākhuga</s> too.
<s>Skanda</s>, <s>Svāmin</s>, <s>Mahāsena</s>, <s>Senānī</s>, and <s>Śikhivāhana</s> are names of <s>Skanda</s>;
<s>Ṣāṇmātura</s>, <s>Brahmacārin</s>, and son of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Umā</s>, and the <s>Kṛttikās</s>;
<s>Dvādaśākṣa</s>, <s>Mahātejas</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, and <s>Guha</s>;
<s>Viśākha</s>, <s>Śaktibhṛt</s>, foe of <s>Krauñca</s> and <s>Tāraka</s>, and <s>Śarāgnibhū</s>.
<s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s>, and <s>Bhṛṅgirīṭi</s> name the attendant with a body of sinew and bone;
<s>Kuṣmāṇḍaka</s>, <s>Kelikila</s>, <s>Nandīśa</s>, <s>Taṇḍu</s>, and <s>Nandin</s> are further attendants.
<s>Brahmā</s> is <s>Druhiṇa</s>, <s>Viriñci</s>, <s>Drughaṇa</s>, <s>Viriñca</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, <s>Aja</s>, <s>Aṣṭaśravaṇa</s>, and <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>;

children.text: kamanaḥ kaviḥ sāttvikavedagarbhau sthaviraḥ śatānandapitāmahau kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kamana</s>, <s>Kavi</s>, <s>Sāttvika</s>, <s>Vedagarbha</s>, <s>Sthavira</s>, <s>Śatānanda</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, and <s>Ka</s>;

children.text: dhātā vidhātā vidhivedhasau dhruvaḥ purāṇago haṃsagaviśvaretasau
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, <s>Vidhi</s>, <s>Vedhas</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Purāṇaga</s>, <s>Haṃsaga</s>, and <s>Viśvaretas</s>;
<s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Caturmukha</s>, <s>Bhavāntakṛt</s>, <s>Jagatkartṛ</s>, and <s>Saroruhāsana</s>.
He is also <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śatadhṛti</s>, <s>Sraṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Surajyeṣṭha</s>, and <s>Viriñcana</s>;
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Lokeśa</s>, and <s>Nābhipadmātmabhū</s> as well.

<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Dāśārha</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, <s>Abdhiśayana</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and <s>Vajendrānuja</s> are names of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
<s>Viṣvaksena</s>, <s>Narāyaṇa</s>, <s>Jalaśaya</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Śrīpati</s>, <s>Daityāri</s>, <s>Purāṇapuruṣa</s>, <s>Yajñapuruṣa</s>, <s>Tārkṣyadhvaja</s>, and <s>Adhokṣaja</s>;
<s>Govinda</s>, <s>Ṣaḍbindu</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, <s>Padmeśaya</s>, and <s>Padmanābha</s>;
<s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Viśvambhara</s>, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, and <s>Viśvarūpa</s>;

children.text: dāmodaraḥ śaurisanātanau vibhuḥ pītāmbaro mārjajinau kumodakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, <s>Vibhu</s>, <s>Pītāmbara</s>, <s>Mārjajina</s>, and <s>Kumodaka</s>;
<s>Trivikrama</s>, <s>Jahnu</s>, <s>Caturbhuja</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Śatāvarta</s>, <s>Gadāgraja</s>, and <s>Svabhū</s>;
<s>Muñjakeśin</s>, <s>Vanamālin</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, <s>Babhru</s>, <s>Śaśabindu</s>, and <s>Vedhas</s>.
<s>Pṛśniśṛṅga</s>, <s>Dharaṇīdhara</s>, <s>Ātmabhū</s>, <s>Pāṇḍavāyana</s>, and <s>Suvarṇabindu</s>.
<s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Devakīsūnu</s> (son of <s>Devakī</s>), <s>Gopendra</s> (lord of cowherds), and <s>Viṣṭaraśravas</s>;
<s>Somasindhu</s>, <s>Jagannātha</s> (lord of the world), and also <s>Govardhanadhara</s> (lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>);
<s>Yadunātha</s> (lord of the <s>Yadus</s>), bearing the mace, the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, the discus, the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and the conch;
<s>Madhu</s>, <s>Dhenuka</s>, <s>Cāṇūra</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and the two <s>Yamalārjunas</s>;
<s>Kālanemi</s>, <s>Hayagrīva</s>, <s>Śakaṭa</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>;
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, <s>Keśin</s>, <s>Mura</s>, <s>Sālva</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, and <s>Rāhu</s>;
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, <s>Kāliya</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, and <s>Bali</s>;
and <s>Śiśupāla</s> are his destined victims; <s>Vainateya</s> is his vehicle.
His conch is <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, his mark is <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and his sword is <s>Nandaka</s>;

children.text: gadā kaumodakī cāpaṃ śārṅgaṃ cakraṃ sudarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his mace is <s>Kaumodakī</s>, his bow <s>Śārṅga</s>, and his discus <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: maṇiḥ syamantako haste bhujamadhye tu kaustubhaḥ
children.translated_text: The jewel in his hand is <s>Syamantaka</s>; <s>Kaustubha</s>, however, is on his chest.
<s>Vasudeva</s> is also called <s>Bhūkaśyapa</s>, <s>Dundura</s>, and <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Halin</s> (plough-bearer), <s>Musalin</s> (club-bearer), <s>Sāttvata</s>, <s>Kāmapāla</s>, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Priyamadhu</s>, <s>Bala</s>, and <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>;
<s>Rukmibhedin</s>, <s>Pralambabhedin</s>, <s>Yamunābhid</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Tālalakṣman</s>, <s>Ekakuṇḍala</s>, <s>Sita</s>, <s>Asita</s>, and <s>Revatīśa</s>.
<s>Baladeva</s>, <s>Balabhadra</s>, <s>Nīlavastra</s> (blue-clad), and <s>Acyutāgraja</s> (elder brother of <s>Acyuta</s>);
his club is <s>Saunanda</s>, and his plough is called <s>Saṃvartaka</s>.

children.text: lakṣmīḥ padmā ramā yā mā tā sā śrīḥ kamalendirā
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Yā</s>, <s>Mā</s>, <s>Tā</s>, <s>Sā</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, and <s>Indirā</s>;
<s>Haripriyā</s> (beloved of <s>Hari</s>), <s>Padmavāsā</s> (lotus-dwelling), and also <s>Kṣīrodatanayā</s> (daughter of the milk ocean).
<s>Madana</s>, <s>Jarābhīru</s> (fearing old age), <s>Anaṅga</s>, <s>Manmatha</s>, <s>Kamana</s>, <s>Kalākeli</s>, <s>Ananyaja</s>, and <s>Aṅgaja</s>;
<s>Madhudīpa</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Madhusārathi</s>, <s>Smara</s>, <s>Viṣamāyudha</s>, <s>Darpaka</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, and <s>Hṛcchaya</s>.
<s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Śrīnandana</s>, <s>Kandarpa</s>, and <s>Puṣpaketana</s>;
flowers are his arrows, bow, and weapons; his enemies are <s>Śambara</s> and <s>Śūrpaka</s>.

children.text: ketanaṃ mīnamakarau bāṇāḥ pañca ratiḥ priyā
children.translated_text: His banner bears the fish and the makara; his arrows are five, and <s>Rati</s> is his beloved.
Mind, erotic passion, resolve, and the self are his source; his friend is <s>Madhu</s> (spring).
His son is <s>Aniruddha</s>; he is <s>Jhaṣāṅka</s>, <s>Uṣeśa</s> (lord of <s>Uṣā</s>), and <s>Brahmasū</s>.
<s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Śālmalī</s>, younger brother of <s>Aruṇa</s>, and vehicle of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
<s>Sauparṇeya</s>, <s>Vainateya</s>, <s>Suparṇa</s>, <s>Sarpārāti</s> (enemy of serpents), <s>Vajrajit</s>, and <s>Vajratuṇḍa</s>;
<s>Pakṣisvāmin</s> (lord of birds), <s>Kāśyapi</s>, <s>Svarṇakāya</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, <s>Kāmāyu</s>, <s>Garutmān</s>, and <s>Sudhāhṛt</s>.
The <s>Buddha</s> is <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, <s>Trikālavid</s> (knower of the three times), and <s>Jina</s>;
<s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Mahābodhi</s>, <s>Ārya</s>, <s>Śāstā</s>, and <s>Tathāgata</s>;
<s>Pañcajñāna</s> (possessing five knowledges), <s>Ṣaḍabhijña</s> (possessing six superknowledges), <s>Daśārha</s>, and <s>Daśabhūmiga</s>;
<s>Catustriṃśajjātakajña</s> (knower of thirty-four births) and <s>Daśapāramitādhara</s> (bearer of the ten perfections);
<s>Dvādaśākṣa</s>, <s>Daśabala</s> (possessing ten powers), <s>Trikāya</s> (three-bodied), <s>Śrīghana</s>, and <s>Advaya</s>;
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, <s>Saṃgupta</s>, <s>Dayākūrca</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>;
<s>Māralokakhajit</s>, <s>Dharmarāja</s>, and <s>Vijñānamātṛka</s>;

children.text: mahāmaitro munīndraśca buddhāḥ syuḥ sapta te tvamī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmaitra</s> and <s>Munīndra</s>; the Buddhas are seven, namely these.
<s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhū</s>, <s>Kakucchanda</s>, and <s>Kāñcana</s>;
<s>Kāśyapa</s>; and the seventh is <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>, <s>Arkabāndhava</s>.
also <s>Rāhulasū</s> (father of <s>Rāhula</s>), <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, and one of the <s>Gautama</s> lineage;
he is the son of <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Śuddhodana</s>, and is also <s>Devadattāpraja</s>.
The <s>asuras</s> are <s>Daityas</s> (sons of <s>Diti</s>), <s>Dānavas</s> (sons of <s>Danu</s>), dwellers in the underworld, and enemies of the gods;
former gods and pupils of <s>Śukra</s>; the <s>Vidyādevīs</s> are sixteen.
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Prajñaptī</s>, <s>Vajraśṛṅkhalā</s>, and <s>Kuliśāṅkuśā</s>;
<s>Cakreśvarī</s>, <s>Naradattā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and that <s>Mahāparā</s>;
<s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Sarvāstra</s>, <s>Mahājvālā</s>, and <s>Mānavī</s>;
<s>Vairoṭyā</s>, <s>Acchuptā</s>, <s>Mānasī</s>, and <s>Mahāmānasikā</s>: these are they.

children.text: vāgbrāhmī bhāratī gaur gīrvāṇī bhāṣā sarasvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Vāk</s> (speech), <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Gauḥ</s>, <s>Gīrvāṇī</s>, <s>Bhāṣā</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: śrutadevī vacanaṃ tu vyāhāro bhāṣitaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrutadevī</s>; an utterance is <s>vacana</s>, <s>vyāhāra</s>, <s>bhāṣita</s>, or <s>vacas</s>.
An expression with its qualifier is an <s>ākhyāta</s>; a <s>vākya</s> (sentence) is one with an ending, and a <s>pada</s> (word) is one with an inflectional ending.
After <s>rāddha</s>, <s>siddha</s>, and <s>kuta</s> at the close, authoritative statement is <s>āptokti</s>, <s>samaya</s>, or <s>āgama</s>.
The canonical limbs are <s>Ācārāṅga</s>, <s>Sūtrakṛta</s>, <s>Sthānāṅga</s>, and <s>Samavāya</s>;
the fifth limb is <s>Bhagavatī</s>, and there is also <s>Jñātadharmakathā</s>;
the decades called <s>Upāsakadaśā</s>, <s>Antakṛddaśā</s>, and <s>Anuttaraupapātikadaśā</s>;
and <s>Praśnavyākaraṇa</s> and <s>Vipākaśruta</s>.
Thus there are eleven <s>aṅgas</s> with their ancillary limbs; the <s>aṅgas</s> are again twelve.
<s>Dṛṣṭivāda</s> is the twelfth; the twelvefold canon is called <s>Gaṇipiṭaka</s>.
<s>Parikarman</s>, <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Pūrvānuyoga</s>, <s>Parvagata</s>, and <s>Cūlikā</s> are the five;
they are divisions of <s>Dṛṣṭivāda</s>; in <s>Pūrvagata</s> there are also fourteen <s>Pūrvas</s>.
The first <s>Pūrva</s> is <s>Utpāda</s>, then <s>Agrāyaṇīya</s>, and then <s>Vīryapravāda</s>;
then <s>Astipravāda</s>, <s>Jñānapravāda</s>, <s>Satyapravāda</s>, <s>Ātmapravāda</s>, and <s>Karmapravāda</s>.
<s>Pratyākhyāna</s>, <s>Vidyāpravāda</s>, and the one named <s>Kalyāṇa</s>;
then <s>Prāṇāvāya</s>, <s>Kriyāviśāla</s>, and <s>Lokabindusāra</s>.
<s>Svādhyāya</s>, <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Āmnāya</s>, <s>Chandas</s>, <s>Veda</s>, and again <s>Trayī</s>;
the Vedas are <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Yajurveda</s>, and <s>Sāmaveda</s>; the <s>Atharvan</s> is an extract from them.
<s>Vedānta</s> means the <s>Upaniṣads</s>; <s>Oṃkāra</s> and <s>Praṇava</s> are equivalent.
<s>Śikṣā</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, <s>Vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>Chandas</s>, <s>Jyotis</s>, and <s>Nirukta</s>;
these are the six <s>aṅgas</s>; <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> is <s>Smṛti</s> or <s>Dharmasaṃhitā</s>.
<s>Ānvīkṣikī</s> is the science of reasoning; <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> is <s>vicāraṇā</s> (inquiry).
<s>Sarga</s> (creation), <s>pratisarga</s> (re-creation), lineage, and the <s>manvantaras</s>;
and the accounts of dynasties and sub-dynasties: a <s>Purāṇa</s> has these five marks.
The six <s>aṅgas</s>, the four Vedas, <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, and <s>Ānvīkṣikī</s>;
<s>Dharmaśāstra</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>: these are the fourteen sciences.
A <s>sūtra</s> is something that makes an indication; a <s>bhāṣya</s> is an elaboration of the meaning stated in a <s>sūtra</s>.
Prastāva and prakaraṇa denote a topic or section; nirukta is etymological explanation, and padabhañjana is the analysis of words.
An āhnika is a resting point among subordinate sections, so called in connection with rapid recitation.
An adhikaraṇa, however, is the establishment of a single line of reasoning.
A vārttika considers the meaning of what has been stated, what has not been stated, and what has been badly stated.
A ṭīkā is a continuous explanation; a pañjikā is an analysis of individual words.
Nibandha and vṛtti are explanatory compositions in their proper senses; saṃgraha is a gathering together.
By this mode of recitation one should also include terms such as pariśiṣṭa and paddhati.
A kārikā indicates much meaning in a brief form of expression.
Kalindikā is a work embracing all learning; a nighaṇṭu is a collection of names.
Itihāsa is an account of what happened long ago; prabahlikā and prahelikā are riddling sayings.
Janaśruti, kiṃvadantī, vārtā, aitihya, and purātanī denote popular tradition or old report.
Vārtā, pravṛtti, vṛttānta, and udanta denote news or an account; āhvaya and abhidhā mean a name.
Gotra, saṃjñā, nāmadheya, ākhyā, āhvā, abhikhyā, and nāman are also words for a name.
Saṃbodhana, āmantraṇa, āhvāna, and abhimantraṇa denote addressing or calling someone.
Ākāraṇa, hava, and hūti are calls; a call made by many people is saṃhūti.
Udāhāra, upodghāta, upanyāsa, and vāṅmukha denote an introductory statement.
Vyavahāra is litigation or dispute; śapatha, śapana, and śapa denote an oath or imprecation.
Uttara and prativacas mean a reply; praśna, pṛcchā, and anuyojana mean a question.
Kathaṃkathikatā is anxious uncertainty; devapraśna and upaśruti denote an oracular inquiry.

children.text: caṭu cāṭu priyaprāyaṃ priyasatyaṃ tu sūnṛtam
children.translated_text: Caṭu and cāṭu are mostly pleasing speech; pleasant truth is called sūnṛta.
Satya, samyak, samīcīna, ṛta, tathya, and yathātatha mean true, correct, or exactly as it is.
Yathāsthita denotes what stands as it really is; alīka, vitatha, and anṛta denote what is false.
Kliṣṭa, saṃkula, and parasparaparāhata describe speech that is obscure, confused, or mutually contradictory.
Sāntva is very sweet conciliatory speech; grāmya and aślīla mean vulgar or indecent; mliṣṭa and asphuṭa mean indistinct.
Grasta is speech with letters or words swallowed; avācya and anakṣara mean unutterable or inarticulate.
Ambūkṛta is muffled speech, sathūtkāra is accompanied by a spitting sound, and nirasta is uttered hastily.
Āmreḍita is a word repeated twice or three times; abaddha means meaningless or incoherent.
Pṛṣṭhamāṃsādana is speaking of someone's faults behind his back.
Mithyābhiyoga and abhyākhyāna mean false accusation; saṃgata and hṛdayaṃgama mean fitting and pleasing to the heart.
Paruṣa, niṣṭhura, and rūkṣa mean harsh; vikruṣṭa and ghoṣaṇā denote loud proclamation.
Uccairghuṣṭa is what is loudly proclaimed; varṇana, īḍā, stava, stotra, stuti, and nuti denote praise.

children.text: ślāghā praśaṃsārthavādaḥ sā tu mithyā vikatthanam
children.translated_text: Ślāghā, praśaṃsā, and arthavāda mean praise; when such praise is false, it is vikatthana, boasting.
Janapravāda and kaulīna denote public rumor; vigāna and vacanīyatā denote reproach or blame.
Avarṇa and upakrośa mean censure; vāda and niḥparyapāta are further terms for hostile denunciation.
Garhaṇā, dhikkriyā, nindā, kutsā, ākṣepa, and jugupsana all denote condemnation or reproach.
Ākrośa, abhīṣaṅga, and ākṣepa mean abusive attack; śāpa is a curse, and kṣāraṇā is corrosive denunciation.
Gāli is hostile speech; āśīḥ is an auspicious utterance or blessing.
Śloka, kīrti, yaśas, abhikhyā, samājñā, and ruśatī denote fame or renown.

children.text: aśubhā vākśubhā kalyā carcarī carbhaṭī same ||
children.translated_text: Aśubhā vāk is inauspicious speech, while śubhā and kalyā are auspicious speech; carcarī and carbhaṭī are equivalent terms.
When an upālambha, a rebuke, is accompanied by blame, it is called paribhāṣaṇa.
Āpṛcchā, ālāpa, and saṃbhāṣa denote conversation; anulāpa is repeated utterance.
Pralāpa is meaningless talk; vilāpa and paridevana are lamentation.
Ullāpa is speech with plaintive intonation; kākuvāk is tone-marked speech, and anyonyokti, saṃlāpa, and saṃkathā are mutual conversation.
Vipralāpa is contradictory speech; apalāpa is denial.
Supralāpa is good speech, suvacana a good saying; speech carrying a message is vācika.
Ājñā and śiṣṭi, together with deśa when formed with prefixes such as nir-, ā-, and ni-, denote order, appointment, or instruction.
Avavāda also means admonition; preṣaṇa is dispatch after summoning, and pratiśāsana is counter-instruction or command.
Saṃvid, saṃdhā, āsthā, abhyupāya, and forms of śrava with prefixes such as sam-, prati-, and ā- denote consent or agreement.
Aṅgīkāra, abhyupagama, pratijñā, and saṃgara likewise denote acceptance, promise, or compact.
The triad of song, dance, and instrumental music is nāṭya; that same triad is also called tauryatrika.
When this is for viewing, it is saṃgīta; in the terminology of the dramatic śāstra it belongs to nāṭyadharmika convention.
Gīta, gāna, geya, gīti, and gāndharva denote song; next comes nartana, dancing.

children.text: naṭanaṃ nṛtyaṃ nṛttaṃ ca lāsyaṃ nāṭyaṃ ca tāṇḍavam ||
children.translated_text: Naṭana, nṛtya, nṛtta, lāsya, nāṭya, and tāṇḍava are terms for forms of dance or dramatic movement.

children.text: maṇḍalena tu yannṛtyaṃ strīṇāṃ hallīsakaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: The dance of women in a circle is called hallīsaka.
In a drinking assembly there is uccatāla, high rhythm; in battle there is vīrajayantikā.
The place for drama is the raṅga, the stage; the preliminary rite is the pūrvaraṅga or upakrama.
Aṅgahāra and aṅgavikṣepa denote movements of the limbs; vyañjaka and abhinaya are equivalent terms for expressive acting.
That abhinaya is fourfold: āhārya is what is produced by ornaments and the like.
Vācika is done by speech, āṅgika by the body, and sāttvika by inner feeling.
Nāṭaka, prakaraṇa, bhāṇa, prahasana, and ḍima are dramatic forms.
Vyāyoga, samavākāra, vīthi, aṅka, and īhāmṛga are also types to be performed.
These are kinds of performable drama; the stage languages are six, beginning with Sanskrit.
<s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Sāttvatī</s>, <s>Kaiśikī</s>, and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> are the vṛttis, or dramatic styles.
Vādya, vāditra, ātodya, tūrya, tūra, and smaradhvaja are terms for musical instruments.
Stringed instruments beginning with the vīṇā are tata; solid instruments beginning with cymbals are ghana.
Hollow wind instruments beginning with the flute are śuṣira; covered drums beginning with the muraja are ānaddha.
The vīṇā is also called ghoṣavatī, vipañcī, and kaṇṭhakūṇikā.
It is also vallakī; when it has seven strings it is called parivādinī.
<s>Śiva</s>'s vīṇā is <s>Nālambī</s>, while <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s is <s>Kacchapī</s>.

children.text: nāradasya tu mahatī gaṇānāṃ tu prabhāvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s>'s vīṇā is <s>Mahatī</s>, and that of the <s>Gaṇas</s> is <s>Prabhāvatī</s>.
<s>Viśvāvasu</s>'s is <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Tumburu</s>'s is <s>Kalāvatī</s>.

children.text: cāṇḍālānāṃ tu kaṇḍolavīṇā cāṇḍālikā ca sā
children.translated_text: The kaṇḍola-vīṇā of the <s>Cāṇḍālas</s> is called <s>Cāṇḍālikā</s>.
Its body is called kolambaka; its binding or covering is upanāha or nibandhana.
Its rod or neck is called daṇḍa or pravāla; the kakubha is called prasevaka.
At its base is the bamboo rod, also called kalikā or kūṇikā.

children.text: kālasya kriyayā mānaṃ tālaḥ sāmyaṃ punarlayaḥ
children.translated_text: Tāla is the measurement of time by action; laya is evenness or tempo.
Druta, vilambita, madhya, ogha, tattva, and ghana are the successive kinds of tempo.
The <s>mṛdaṅga</s>, or <s>muraja</s>, is threefold: <s>āṅkya</s>, <s>āliṅgya</s>, and <s>ūrdhvaka</s>.
There is the <s>yaśaḥpaṭaha</s>; also <s>ḍhakkā</s>, <s>bherī</s>, <s>dundubhi</s>, and <s>ānaka</s> are drums.
The <s>paṭaha</s> is another drum; then <s>śārikā</s> or <s>koṇa</s> is the implement for playing the <s>vīṇā</s> and the like.
The rasas include <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), and <s>bhayānaka</s> (fearful),
as well as <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous), and <s>śānta</s> (peaceful); these are the <s>rasas</s>. The <s>bhāvas</s>, in turn, are threefold,
through the divisions of <s>sthāyin</s> (stable), <s>sāttvika</s>, and <s>saṃcārin</s> (transitory); and <s>rati</s> (love), in turn,
is <s>rāga</s>, <s>anurāga</s>, and <s>anurati</s>; <s>hāsa</s> is <s>hasana</s> and <s>hasa</s>.
<s>Gharghara</s>, <s>hāsikā</s>, and <s>hāsya</s> denote laughter; among these, <s>smita</s> is a smile in which the teeth are not seen.
<s>Vakroṣṭikā</s> is a crooked-lipped smile, and <s>hasita</s> is when the buds of the teeth are slightly visible.
<s>Vihasita</s> is when a slight sound is heard; <s>aṭṭahāsa</s> is loud laughter.
<s>Atihāsa</s> is laughter that is excessive or prolonged; <s>apahāsa</s> is laughter produced without cause.
When it includes mockery it is <s>āchuritaka</s>; <s>hasana</s> is laughter with quivering lips.

children.text: śokaḥ śukśocanaṃ khedaḥ krodho manyuḥ krudhā ruṣā
children.translated_text: <s>Śoka</s> (grief) is <s>śuk</s>, <s>śocana</s>, and <s>kheda</s>; <s>krodha</s> (anger) is <s>manyu</s>, <s>krudh</s>, and <s>ruṣ</s>.

children.text: krutkopaḥ pratigho roṣo ruṭ cotsāhaḥ pragalbhatā
children.translated_text: Anger is also <s>krut</s>, <s>kopa</s>, <s>pratigha</s>, <s>roṣa</s>, and <s>ruṭ</s>; <s>utsāha</s> is boldness.
<s>Abhiyoga</s>, <s>udyama</s>, <s>prauḍhi</s>, <s>udyoga</s>, and <s>kiyadetikā</s> are names for exertion.
<s>Adhyavasāya</s> and <s>ūrj</s> are also energy; when that is accompanied by excellence, it is <s>vīrya</s>.
Fear is <s>bhaya</s>, <s>bhī</s>, <s>bhīti</s>, <s>ātaṅka</s>, <s>āśaṅkā</s>, <s>sādhvasa</s>, and <s>dara</s>.
It is also <s>bhiyā</s>; that fear may arise from serpents, from kings, or from one's own side.
Fear from fire, water, and the like is unseen; fear born from one's own or an enemy army is seen.
<s>Bhayaṃkara</s>, <s>pratibhaya</s>, <s>bhīma</s>, <s>bhīṣma</s>, and <s>bhayānaka</s> mean fearsome.

children.text: bhīṣaṇaṃ bhairavaṃ ghoraṃ dāruṇaṃ ca bhayāvaham
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>bhairava</s>, <s>ghora</s>, <s>dāruṇa</s>, and <s>bhayāvaha</s> also mean terrifying.
<s>Jugupsā</s> is <s>ghṛṇā</s> (disgust); then <s>vismaya</s> (wonder) is <s>citra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s>.
<s>Codya</s> and <s>āścarya</s> denote wonder; <s>śama</s> is <s>śānti</s>, and also <s>śamatha</s> and <s>upaśama</s>.
It is the destruction of craving; these are the stable states, in order, as the causes of the rasas.

children.text: stambho jāḍyaṃ svedo gharmanidāghau pulakaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Stambha</s> (stupefaction) is <s>jāḍya</s>; <s>sveda</s> (sweat) is <s>gharma</s> and <s>nidāgha</s>; <s>pulaka</s>, in turn,
is <s>romāñca</s>, <s>kaṇṭaka</s>, <s>romavikāra</s>, and <s>romaharṣaṇa</s>.
It is also <s>romodgama</s>, <s>uddhuṣaṇa</s>, and <s>ullukasana</s>.
<s>Svarabheda</s> is <s>kallatva</s> (alteration of the voice); trembling in the voice is <s>vepathu</s>.
<s>Vaivarṇya</s> (change of color) is <s>kālikā</s>; <s>aśru</s> (tears) is <s>bāṣpa</s>, <s>netrāmbu</s>, and <s>rodana</s>.
<s>Asra</s> and <s>asru</s> also mean tears; <s>pralaya</s> is lack of movement. These are the eight <s>sāttvika</s> states.

children.text: dhṛtiḥ saṃtoṣaḥ svāsthyaṃ syādādhyānaṃ smaraṇaṃ smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛti</s> is contentment and composure; <s>ādhyāna</s> is recollection and memory.
<s>Mati</s>, <s>manīṣā</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>dhī</s>, <s>dhiṣaṇā</s>, <s>jñapti</s>, and <s>cetanā</s> denote intelligence.
<s>Pratibhā</s>, <s>pratipat</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, <s>prekṣā</s>, <s>cit</s>, and <s>upalabdhi</s> also denote understanding.

children.text: saṃvittiḥ śemuṣī dṛṣṭiḥ sā medhā dhāraṇakṣamā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃvitti</s>, <s>śemuṣī</s>, and <s>dṛṣṭi</s> do likewise; <s>medhā</s> is the capacity for retention.
<s>Paṇḍā</s> is insight following reality; with regard to liberation it is <s>jñāna</s>, and elsewhere <s>vijñāna</s>.

children.text: śuśrūṣā śravaṇaṃ caiva grahaṇaṃ dhāraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śuśrūṣā</s>, hearing, grasping, and retention,
conjecture and exclusion, understanding of meaning, and knowledge of reality are qualities of the intellect.
<s>Vrīḍā</s>, <s>lajjā</s>, <s>mandākṣa</s>, <s>hrī</s>, <s>trapā</s>, and <s>sāpatrapā</s> denote shame or embarrassment.
<s>Jāḍya</s> is stupidity; <s>viṣāda</s> is <s>avasāda</s>, <s>sāda</s>, and <s>viṣaṇṇatā</s>.
<s>Mada</s> is <s>unmoha</s> and <s>saṃbheda</s>; disease is <s>ādhi</s> and a producer of pain.
Sleep is <s>nidrā</s>, <s>pramīlā</s>, <s>śayana</s>, <s>saṃveśa</s>, <s>svāpa</s>, and <s>saṃlaya</s>.
<s>Nandīmukhī</s> and <s>śvāsaheti</s> are terms connected with drowsiness; <s>supta</s> is <s>sādhikā</s>.
<s>Autsukya</s> (eagerness) is <s>raṇaraṇaka</s> and <s>utkaṇṭhā</s>; <s>āyallakā</s> and <s>arati</s>,
as well as <s>hṛllekhā</s> and <s>utkalikā</s>, are uneasiness; then <s>avahitthā</s> is concealment of one's outward expression.
<s>Śaṅkā</s> is the imagining of something undesirable; <s>cāpala</s> is instability.
<s>Ālasya</s> is <s>tandrā</s> and <s>kausīdya</s>; <s>harṣa</s> is gladness of mind.
<s>Hlāda</s>, <s>pramoda</s>, <s>pramada</s>, <s>mut</s>, <s>prīti</s>, <s>āmoda</s>, and <s>saṃmada</s> denote joy.
<s>Ānanda</s> and <s>ānandathu</s> also denote joy; <s>garva</s> is <s>ahaṃkāra</s> and <s>avilaptatā</s>.
<s>Darpa</s>, <s>abhimāna</s>, <s>mamatā</s>, <s>māna</s>, <s>cittonnati</s>, and <s>smaya</s> are pride.
When that pride is mutual it is <s>ahamahamikā</s>; when it concerns one's own self-estimation,
arising from pride, it is <s>sāhopuruṣikā</s>; again <s>ahaṃpūrvikā</s>
is the thought, 'I first, I first'; <s>ugratva</s> is <s>caṇḍatā</s> (fierceness).
<s>Prabodha</s> is wakefulness; <s>glāni</s> is weakness of strength.

children.text: dainyaṃ kārpaṇyaṃ śramastu klamaḥ kleśaḥ pariśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dainya</s> is <s>kārpaṇya</s>; <s>śrama</s> is <s>klama</s>, <s>kleśa</s>, and <s>pariśrama</s>.
<s>Prayāsa</s>, <s>āyāsa</s>, and <s>vyāyāma</s> also denote exertion; <s>unmāda</s> is derangement of mind.
<s>Moha</s> is bewilderment; <s>cintā</s> is brooding thought; <s>amarṣa</s> arises from anger.
A spirited quality is one possessed of desire to conquer and energy; <s>trāsa</s> is sudden fear.
<s>Apasmāra</s> is a seizure; <s>nirveda</s> is self-disparagement.
<s>Āvega</s> is haste: <s>tvari</s>, <s>tūrṇi</s>, <s>saṃvega</s>, <s>saṃbhrama</s>, and <s>tvarā</s>.
<s>Vitarka</s> is conjectural inference, <s>parāmarśa</s>, and <s>vimarśana</s>.
<s>Adhyāhāra</s>, <s>tarka</s>, and <s>ūha</s> are reasoning; <s>asūyā</s> is fault-finding with another's qualities.
<s>Mṛti</s>, <s>saṃsthā</s>, <s>mṛtyu</s>, <s>kāla</s>, <s>paralokagama</s>, and <s>atyaya</s> denote death.
<s>Pañcatva</s>, <s>nidhana</s>, <s>nāśa</s>, <s>dīrghanidrā</s>, and <s>nimīlana</s> also denote death.
<s>Diṣṭānta</s>, <s>asta</s>, <s>kāladharma</s>, and <s>avasāna</s> do likewise; death is universal.
<s>Maraka</s> and <s>māri</s> are also terms for death or destruction; these thirty-three are the <s>vyabhicāriṇs</s> (transitory states).

children.text: syuḥ kāraṇāni kāryāṇi sahacārīṇi yāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Those things which are causes, effects, and accompanying factors
of stable states such as love in the ordinary world, when they occur in drama and poetry,
are called <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicāriṇs</s>.

children.text: vyaktaḥ sa tairvibhāvādyaiḥ sthāyī bhāvo bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: The stable emotion, manifested by these <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like, becomes <s>rasa</s>.
In drama, the authorized characters are <s>pātras</s>; each one's costume or role is a <s>bhūmikā</s>.
An actor is called <s>śailūṣa</s>, <s>bharata</s>, <s>sarvakeśī</s>, and <s>bharataputraka</s>.
He is also <s>dhātrīputra</s>, one who lives by the stage, and <s>raṅgāvatāraka</s>.
<s>Naṭa</s>, <s>kṛśāśvī</s>, and <s>śailālī</s> are actor-terms; <s>cāraṇa</s> is <s>kuśīlava</s>.
<s>Bhrabhrubhrūbhṛpara</s> and <s>kuṃsa</s> denote an actor who wears women's costume.
A <s>veśyācārya</s> is a <s>pīṭhamarda</s>; a <s>sūtradhāra</s> is a <s>sūcaka</s>.

children.text: nandī tu pāṭhako nāndyāḥ pārśvasthaḥ pāripārśvikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The reciter of the <s>nāndī</s> benediction is a <s>pāṭhaka</s>; a side-attendant is a <s>pāripārśvika</s>.
Vāsantika, kelikila, vaihāsika, and vidūṣaka are terms for a jester.
Prahāsī and prītida are also such terms; next, ṣiṅga and pallavaka denote a viṭa, a gallant.
Āvuka denotes a father, while āvutta and bhāvuka denote a sister’s husband.
Bhāva means a learned man; kumāra and bhartṛdāraka denote a crown prince.

children.text: bālā vāsūrmārṣa āryo devo bhaṭṭārako nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Bālā denotes a young girl; vāsū, mārṣa, and ārya are respectful forms, and deva and bhaṭṭāraka denote a king.
Rāṣṭrīya means the king’s brother-in-law; a daughter is called bhartṛdārikā.
A consecrated queen is devī, another queen is bhaṭṭinī, and a courtesan is ajjukā.
Haṇḍe, hañje, and halā are respectively calls to a low woman, a maidservant, and a female friend.
Abrahmaṇya is uttered in reference to one who must not be killed; an elder sister is svasāttikā.
A husband is āryaputra, a mother is ambā, and bhadantas are Buddhists and the like.
For a venerable person, tatrabhavān, atrabhavān, and bhagavān may be used.
Pāda, bhaṭṭāraka, and deva are to be employed as honorific names.
Martya, pañcajana, bhūspṛk, puruṣa, pūruṣa, and nara denote a human being.

children.text: mānuṣo nā viṭ manujo mānavaḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: Mānuṣa, nā, viṭ, manuja, mānava, and pumān likewise mean a man or human being.

children.text: bālaḥ pākaḥ śiśurḍimbhaḥ potaḥ śāvaḥ stanaṃdhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Bāla, pāka, śiśu, ḍimbha, pota, śāva, and stanaṃdhaya denote a child or infant.
Pṛthuka, arbha, uttānaśaya, kṣīrakaṇṭha, and kumāraka are further terms for a child.
Śiśutva, śaiśava, and bālya denote childhood; vayastha, taruṇa, and yuvā denote a youth.

children.text: tāruṇyaṃ yauvanaṃ vṛddhaḥ pravayāḥ sthaviro jaran ||
children.translated_text: Tāruṇya and yauvana denote youth; vṛddha, pravayas, sthavira, and jaran denote an old man.

children.text: jarī jīrṇo yātayāmo jīno 'tha visrasā jarā
children.translated_text: Jarī, jīrṇa, yātayāma, and jīna mean aged; then visrasā and jarā denote old age.
Vārdhaka and sthāvira also denote old age; jyāyān, varṣīyān, and daśamī mean older or elder.
Vidvān, sudhī, kavi, vicakṣaṇa, labdhavarṇa, jña, prāptarūpa, kṛtin, kṛṣṭi, abhirūpa, and dhīra denote a learned or intelligent person.
Medhāvin, kovida, viśārada, sūri, doṣajña, prājña, paṇḍita, manīṣin, budha, and prabuddha likewise denote a wise person.
Vyakta, vipaścit, saṃkhyāvān, and san are terms for one who knows; for an expert there is śikṣita.
Niṣṇāta, nipuṇa, dakṣa, karmahasta, karmamukha, and kṛtin also denote a skilled person.
Kuśala, catura, abhijña, vijña, vaijñānika, and paṭu mean skillful or clever.
Cheka denotes a vidagdha, a clever and refined person; prauḍha, pragalbha, and pratibhāmukha denote one who is confident or ready-witted.
Kuśāgrīyamati and sūkṣmadarśin denote a sharp and subtle thinker; tatkāladhī means quick-minded.
Pratyutpannamati means one whose wit is ready; one who sees from afar is dīrghadarśin.
Hṛdayālu, sahṛdaya, and cidrūpa denote a person of feeling or sensibility; then, for a cultured person,
vyutpanna, prahata, and kṣuṇṇa are used; antarvāṇi means one versed in śāstra.
Vāgīśa means lord of speech; vāgmī, vācoyuktipaṭu, and pravāk denote an eloquent speaker.
Samukha and vāvadūka are further terms; vada, vaktṛ, and vadāvada denote a speaker.
Jalpāka, vācāla, vācāṭa, and bahugarhyavāk denote a talkative or much-censured speaker.
Yadvada denotes one who has no reply; durvāk and advada denote bad speech, and adhara means an inferior speaker.
For a poor speaker there are eḍamūka and aneḍamūka; avāk and aśruta denote one without speech or without being heard.
Ravaṇa and śabdana are equivalent, and kuvāda and kucara are likewise the same.
Lohala means one whose speech is indistinct; mūka and avāk mean mute, and asvara means one with an unpleasant voice.
Veditṛ, vidura, and vindu denote a knower; vandāru means one who salutes.
Āśaṃsu denotes one who wishes or praises; kaṭvara means extremely contemptible.
Nirākariṣṇu and kṣipnu denote one who rejects or casts aside; vikāsī is the same as vikasvara, expanding or blooming.
Durmukha, mukhara, and ābaddhamukha denote a foul- or loud-mouthed person; śalka means pleasant-spoken.
One whose habit is giving is vadānya or vadanya; next comes the foolish person.

children.text: mūḍho mando yathājāto bālo mātṛmukho jaḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Mūḍha, manda, yathājāta, bāla, mātṛmukha, and jaḍa denote a foolish or dull person.
Mūrkha, amedha, vivarṇa, ajña, vaidheya, and mātṛśāsita are further terms for a fool.
Devānāṃpriya and jālma also denote such a fool; dīrghasūtra means one slow in action.
One sluggish in actions is kuṇṭha; one active in tasks is kriyāvān or karmasu udyata.
Karmakṣama and alaṃkarmīṇa mean capable of work; karmaśūra and karmaṭha mean energetic in work.
Karmaśīla, kārma, āyaḥśūlika, and tīkṣṇakarmakṛt denote one whose work is hard or vigorous.
Siṃhasaṃhanana means lion-built, and svaṅga means well-limbed; svatantra and niravagraha mean independent.
Yathākāmī, svaruci, svacchanda, svairin, and apāvṛta denote one who acts according to his own wish.
Yadṛcchā, svairitā, and svecchā mean free choice; one who has a lord is nāthavān, nighna, or gṛhyaka.
Tantrāyatta, vaśa, adhīna, and chandavant denote one dependent on another.
Lakṣmīvant, lakṣmaṇa, śrīla, ibhya, āḍhya, dhanī, and īśvara denote a wealthy or prosperous person.
For prosperity, the terms are vibhūti, saṃpatti, lakṣmī, śrī, ṛddhi, and saṃpad.
Daridra, durvidha, duḥstha, durgata, niḥsva, and kīkaṭa denote a poor person.
Akiṃcana is another such term; adhipa, īśa, netṛ, parivṛḍha, and adhibhū denote a ruler or master.
Pati, indra, svāmin, nātha, ārya, prabhu, bhartṛ, īśvara, and vibhu also denote a lord.
Īśitṛ and nāyaka are further terms for a master; niyojya means a servant or attendant.
Ḍiṅgara, kiṃkara, bhṛtya, ceṭa, gopya, and parācita denote a servant.
Dāsa, preṣya, pariskanda, bhujiṣya, and parikarman are further terms for a servant.
Parānna, paripiṇḍāda, parajāta, and paraidhita denote one maintained by another’s food or support.
For a hired servant, bhṛtibhuj, vaitanika, and karmakara are also used.

children.text: sa nirvṛtiḥ karmakaro bhṛtiḥ syānniṣkrayaḥ paṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The hired worker is also called nirvṛti and karmakara; bhṛti, niṣkraya, and paṇa denote payment.

children.text: karmaṇyā vetanaṃ mūlyaṃ nirveśo bharaṇaṃ vidhā ||
children.translated_text: For work done, vetana, mūlya, nirveśa, bharaṇa, and vidhā denote wages or price.

children.text: bharmaṇyā bharma bhṛtyā ca bhogastu gaṇikābhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Bharmaṇyā, bharma, and bhṛtyā are further terms for hire; bhoga is a courtesan’s fee.
Khalapū means a worker who does many tasks; a bearer of burdens is bhārika.
For a carrier of goods there is vaivadhika; for a burden, the words are vivadha and vīvadha.
Kāca and śikya denote the carrying sling; its support is the carrying pole, bhārayaṣṭi or vihaṅgikā.
Śūra, ārabhaṭa, vīra, and vikrānta denote a brave man; then come terms for a coward.
Kātara, daridra, cakita, bhīta, bhīru, bhīruka, and bhīluka denote a fearful or timid person.
Vihasta and vyākula mean agitated or distracted; kāṃdiśīka means one fleeing from fear.
